newsitem.title: USA: Spiegel aims to improve catalog operation.
newsitem.headline: Spiegel aims to improve catalog operation.

text.p: Spiegel Inc said Wednesday that it hopes to improve productivity in its catalog division, which depressed results for the first quarter.
Spiegel said its Eddie Bauer business was favorable in the first quarter, driven by strong sales and margin performance.

"Our plan for 1997 includes opening up to 70 Eddie Bauer stores, improving the productivity of our Spiegel Catalog business and launching new credit programs which will enhance credit options supporting our merchandising strategies," John Shea, vice chairman, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
"Spiegal Catalog will continue to be challenged during this period of transition," Shea added. "However, I am confident that the actions being taken will improve our performance."
He said Eddie Bauer is Spiegel's largest segment, accounting for about 55 percent of annualized sales.
Earlier, Spiegel reported a first quarter loss of $0.28 a share, compared with a year-ago loss of $0.13 after a $0.04 gain. Revenues were $601.8 million, down from $634.7 million.
Total catalog sales dropped nine percent, while total retail sales increased eight percent in the quarter, Spiegel said. Comparable store sales for Eddie Bauer rose four percent in the quarter.
The company said the catalog division was hurt by lower productivity from mailings and the impact on sales from tightened credit policies.

"Spiegel Catalog experienced negative sales and earnings trends," Shea said. "Spiegel Catalog is in a period of transition, implementing new business strategies aimed at repositioning its merchandise offering and catalog presentation in an effort to maximize the productivity of its customer base."
